title: One-on-one: PM <> Eng Lead — agenda & follow-ups (API / Console / Dedicated / Private)
content:
Meeting: weekly 1:1 with Eng Lead (Omar) — quick cadence for exec prep and rollout blockers
Date: 2025-11-19 (prep for standup with GTM)
Duration: 30m
Location: Zoom / async notes in Drive
Goal: Align on immediate blockers across API, Console, Dedicated/Private launches; agree owners for canary and regression actions; decide on go/no-go signals for Dedicated capacity bump.

Top priorities to bring up (2–3):
- Dedicated capacity commit negotiation: confirm whether we proceed with 3-month burst pool while infra autoscaler work lands. Need decision thresholds (latency + utilization) for trigger. (JIRA: INFR-4823)
- Console rollout: post-canary issues — command palette latency spike in regions eu-west1. Root cause suspected in client-side batching change (PR 1024). Decide rollback vs patch.
- Private deploy packaging: KMS integration docs are missing step-by-step; security wants an artifact for audit. Decide owner to produce minimal compliance checklist by EOW.

Agenda (fast, focused):
1) 5m - Quick status: any new showstoppers since last sync?
2) 10m - Dedicated capacity decision: numbers, risks, fallback plan
3) 10m - Console canary & PR 1024 status + rollback criteria
4) 5m - Private/KMS audit checklist + action owners

Prep notes (things I want Omar to surface):
- Any SRE objections to temporary capacity commit? Costs vs SLOs tradeoff — ask for concrete SLIs we can measure quickly.
- Time estimate for autoscaler fix (is the patch ready to test in staging? can we run a 2-hour soak?)
- Are we comfortable with cross-region fallback policy (route to hosted API when dedicated pool saturated)? What cost impact does that have?

Quick data points to drop in meeting:
- Last 24h p95 token latency for hosted API: 380ms (steady), for console-backed routes: p95 620ms (spike correlated with 11:00–13:00 UTC deployments)
- Dedicated pool utilization (staging): 67% avg, 92% peak during synthetic test at 2025-11-15 14:22 UTC
- Expected Q4 burst spend estimate if we add 2x GPUs for 3 months: ~$48k (finance ok with contingency if we get exec signoff)

Risks / Context to call out:
- If we decline the short-term capacity commit and pull back canary, customer-facing latency regressions could increase support tickets for 2–4 key accounts (list attached in Confluence).
- KMS packaging delay blocks a single enterprise proof-of-concept; legal wants a signed delivery timeline.

Decisions needed in this 1:1 (explicit asks):
- Approve 3-month Dedicated burst pool purchase if autoscaler fix cannot be validated in 72h. (Decision: yes/no)
- Approve rollback of PR 1024 for Console routes until we have a client-side fix and one successful canary cycle. (Decision: rollback/hold)
- Assign owner for KMS audit checklist and target date (who will produce artifact?).

Action items (post-meeting to capture in tracker) — draft assignments:
- Claudia: prepare short one-pager for exec with cost vs SLO scenarios for Dedicated commit (due 2025-11-20)
- Omar (Eng Lead): authorize temporary burst if autoscaler test fails or provide exact ETA for autoscaler fix (update by 2025-11-21)
- Jin (SRE): run 2-hour autoscaler soak in staging and share logs (JIRA: INFR-4823, due 2025-11-21)
- Elena (Security): draft minimal KMS checklist + list of missing artefacts for audit (due 2025-11-22)
- Omar + Claudia: decide rollback plan for PR 1024 tonight if canary shows repeat spike (contingency plan doc link to be created)

Notes to self / corollary items to surface during meeting:
- Bring up Metric: # of routed fallbacks to hosted API last 48h and which customers were impacted (we need to prioritize)
- Ask Omar about capacity reservations for Private customers — is there a simple toggle in our control plane to reserve N GPUs per customer? (If not, add to backlog)
- Confirm whether Dedicated SLA language needs tweak for burst economics (legal signoff timeline)

Parking lot / future topics (mention but do not block on now):
- Eval harness for regression alerts tied to prompt sets (product-optimize): we should blueprint next quarter; can pair with reliability team
- Long-term: consider feature-flagging client-side batching at console to avoid whole-service rolling changes

Open questions I want answered in the 1:1:
- What are the exact signal thresholds for triggering the fallback policy (latency p95 > X for Y minutes)? Who owns tuning these values?
- If we purchase burst GPUs, who owns provisioning and cost center tagging? (ops vs finance?)
- Does the Private on-prem package need an updated installer for KMS v2? If yes, what is the rough ETA?

Conversation starters (one-liners to get to decisions quickly):
- "If autoscaler isn't healthy by EOD Friday, I recommend we sign the 3-month burst to protect key customers — can you commit to that?"
- "For PR 1024, do we have logs that prove the client change is the root cause? If not, we rollback now and investigate upstream."

Follow-up note format (what I'll update after the 1:1):
- Decisions made (Y/N + brief rationale)
- New action items with owners + due dates (I will move these into API-ops tracker)
- Any immediate comms (draft an email/Slack message for affected customers + internal triage channel)

Draft Slack comms snippet (if we approve temporary capacity):
- ":loudspeaker: Quick ops update — we've approved a temporary Dedicated burst pool to stabilize latency for select accounts while autoscaler fixes are validated. ETA: booked for next 24–48h, finance notified. We'll share more once tests complete."

Quick scratch reminders (personal):
- Bring data export for last 7 days fallback hits (CSV) to attach to exec one-pager
- Prep short list of 3 customers most impacted by Console latency to pre-brief CS and AE teams
- Keep the ask concrete: desired outcome should be either "authorize burst" or "authorize rollback" — avoid open-ended requests

End of notes.

---
Revision log:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft (agenda + open questions)
- 2025-11-15: added utilization numbers after staging run
- 2025-11-18: updated owner assignments and target dates after async check-ins
